name: @kitora/ai-chat
description: Kitora's AI chat UI: a framework-free chat core (message tree with branches, stream folding, streaming-safe markdown, a pluggable adapter seam with a scripted fake) with React bindings and styled parts: transcript, composer with attachments and slash commands, tool-call cards, agent step traces, a context-usage meter, a model selector, citations, reasoning, artifacts panel, conversation list.

exports.name: JsonValue
exports.description: Any value JSON can carry: tool arguments and tool results are this, never `unknown` blobs.

exports.name: ChatRole
exports.description: Who wrote a message: `user`, `assistant` or `system`.

exports.name: TextPart
exports.description: Plain or markdown text; the assistant's streams in through `text-delta` chunks.

exports.name: ReasoningPart
exports.description: The model's visible thinking, shown folded; `done` flips when the answer starts.

exports.name: ToolStatus
exports.description:
Lifecycle of one tool call, in order: `pending` (the model asked, nothing ran yet, e.g. waiting
for approval) → `running` → `result` or `error`. A call may skip `pending` and start `running`.

exports.name: ToolCallPart
exports.description: One tool call in a reply: its name, arguments, lifecycle status, and result or error.

exports.name: Source
exports.description: One cited document; the text cites it by its 1-based position as `[1]`.

exports.name: SourcesPart
exports.description: The documents a reply cites; the text points at them as `[1]`, `[2]`.

exports.name: ArtifactKind
exports.description: What an artifact holds, which decides how its panel previews it.

exports.name: Artifact
exports.description: A standalone piece of output (a file, a page, a document) opened beside the chat.

exports.name: ArtifactPart
exports.description: A reference from a message to an artifact; the artifact's body lives in the part so a thread is self-contained.

exports.name: MessagePart
exports.description: One typed piece of a message: text, reasoning, a tool call, sources or an artifact.

exports.name: Attachment
exports.description: A file the user attached; `url` is whatever the host can show (an object URL, a CDN link).

exports.name: MessageStatus
exports.description: `streaming` while chunks arrive; `stopped` when the user hit Stop; `error` when the stream failed.

exports.name: Feedback
exports.description: A rating on an assistant reply: thumbs `up` or `down`.

exports.name: ChatMessage
exports.description: One message of a conversation, made of typed parts, with its parent in the thread tree.

exports.name: ChatChunk
exports.description: One unit of an adapter's stream; `applyChunk` folds each into the streaming assistant message.

exports.name: ChatRequest
exports.description: What the store hands an adapter: the active path up to (not including) the reply being generated.

exports.name: ChatAdapter
exports.description:
The one seam to a backend. Anything that can turn a request into an async stream of chunks works:
a fetch to an SSE endpoint, a WebSocket, a local model, the scripted fake. Stop is the `signal`
aborting; an adapter should end its iterator promptly when it does.

exports.description: Type guard for arrays; `Array.isArray` alone does not narrow a readonly array type.

exports.name: jsonObject
exports.description: The value as an object, or null for arrays, primitives and undefined.

exports.name: JsonObject
exports.description: A JSON object: string keys to JSON values.

exports.name: pathTo

exports.name: siblingsOf
exports.description: The siblings of a message (the alternatives at its fork) and its position among them.

exports.name: selectBranch
exports.description: Makes `id` the selected alternative at its fork; its own selected descendants come back with it.

exports.name: stepBranch
exports.description: Steps to the previous (-1) or next (+1) alternative of `id`, clamped at the ends.

exports.name: threadFrom
exports.description: Builds a thread from a linear list (each message's parentId must point at the one before).

exports.name: ROOT_KEY
exports.description: Key of the virtual parent of first messages in `children` / `selected`.

exports.name: ChatThread
exports.description: A conversation as a tree of messages, with the selected child at every fork; the visible conversation follows those selections.

exports.name: emptyThread
exports.description: A thread with no messages.

exports.name: Siblings
exports.description: Where a message sits among its alternatives: 0-based `index` of `count`, plus the ids in order.

exports.name: applyChunk
exports.description: One stream step; `now` stamps tool start and end times.
exports.signature: (message: ChatMessage, chunk: ChatChunk, now?: number) => ChatMessage

exports.name: finalizeMessage
exports.description:
Settles a message whose stream ended: open reasoning closes, tool calls still

exports.name: messageText
exports.description: The message's plain text (its text parts joined), what Copy puts on the clipboard.

exports.name: parseMarkdown
exports.description: Parses markdown into blocks; tolerant of half-written input, so a streaming reply renders as it arrives.

exports.description: Parses one line's inline markdown (code, bold, italic, strike, links, bare URLs, citations); unsafe link schemes stay text.

exports.name: Inline

exports.name: TableAlign

exports.name: ListItem
exports.description: One item of a parsed markdown list, with its task checkbox state.

exports.name: Block
exports.description: One block of parsed markdown: paragraph, heading, code (`open` while its fence is unclosed), list, quote, table or rule.

exports.name: slashQuery
exports.description:
The slash query under the caret, or null when there is none. A command is
typed at the very start of the message (`/sum|`) and ends at the first space,
so `/summarize this` past the space is plain text again.

exports.name: matchCommands
exports.description: Commands matching `query`: name prefix first, then name or description containing it; stable within each tier.

exports.name: applyCommand
exports.description: The text after the composer picks `command`: the command, a space, and whatever followed the old query.

exports.name: formatBytes
exports.description: "1.2 MB", "340 KB", "12 B": short sizes for attachment chips.

exports.name: rejectAttachment

exports.signature: (file: { readonly name: string; readonly size: number; readonly type: string; }, existing: number, rules?: AttachmentRules) => string | null

exports.name: SlashCommand
exports.description: A command the composer's `/` menu offers, with its description and optional hint and group.

exports.name: AttachmentRules
exports.description: The size, count and type limits files must pass to be attached.

exports.name: DEFAULT_MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES

exports.name: DEFAULT_MAX_ATTACHMENTS

exports.name: groupConversations
exports.description: Groups (newest first inside each); empty groups are left out. `now` makes it testable; days and months fall in `timeZone` (the system's when omitted).

exports.name: ConversationSummary

exports.name: ConversationGroup

exports.name: ChatStatus

exports.name: SendInput
exports.description: What the user sends: the text and any attachments.

exports.description: The framework-free chat controller: owns a thread, runs the adapter and folds its stream into the reply; send, stop, regenerate, edit, branch and feedback go through it.

exports.name: sleep
exports.description: Resolves after `ms`, or rejects with an AbortError as soon as `signal` aborts.

exports.name: tokenize
exports.description: Splits text into word-sized deltas that keep their whitespace, the way model tokens arrive.

exports.name: lastUserText

exports.description: Creates a `ChatAdapter` that streams scripted replies with realistic timing, for demos and tests; nothing leaves the page.

exports.name: ScriptedAdapterOptions

exports.description: Pause between streamed deltas, in ms, when `tokenDelayMs` is not set.

exports.name: DEFAULT_FIRST_TOKEN_MS
exports.description: Pause before the first chunk, in ms, when `firstTokenMs` is not set.

exports.name: createAttachmentId
exports.description: A process-unique attachment id: time base plus a counter, so two files picked in one tick never collide.

exports.name: autosizeTextarea
exports.description: Grows `el` to fit its content up to `maxPx`, then lets it scroll.

exports.name: downloadText
exports.description: Saves `content` as a file named `fileName` through a temporary link.

exports.name: AttachmentAdapter
exports.description:
The seam between a picked File and the `Attachment` a message carries. The default keeps the
file local (an object URL for images); a host that uploads first (S3, a CDN, its own API)
returns the remote URL instead. `release` frees whatever `fromFile` allocated when a chip is
removed before sending.

exports.name: FALLBACK_MIME
exports.description: MIME used when the browser reports none (unknown extensions report "").

exports.name: objectUrlAttachments
exports.description: The default adapter: no upload, an object URL for images so the chip can show a thumbnail.

exports.name: createStickToBottom
exports.description:
Keeps `scroller` pinned to its bottom while `content` grows, lets go the moment the reader scrolls
UP, sticks again at the bottom, and keeps the reader's place when content above them changes.
Layout changes that move scrollTop without the reader (a narrower pane) never unstick it.
exports.signature: (scroller: HTMLElement, content: HTMLElement, options?: StickToBottomOptions) => StickToBottom

exports.name: STICK_THRESHOLD_PX
exports.description: Within this many px of the bottom counts as "at the bottom", so sub-pixel layout never unsticks.

exports.name: StickToBottom
exports.description: A scroller kept pinned to its newest content while the reader is at the bottom, from `createStickToBottom`.

exports.name: StickToBottomOptions
exports.description: Options for `createStickToBottom`.

exports.name: useControllable
exports.description:
`[value, setValue, getLatest]`: reads `value` when the caller passes one (controlled) and its own
state otherwise. `setValue` always reports through `onChange`; uncontrolled, it also updates.
`getLatest` returns the newest value, including one set earlier in the same event before React
re-rendered (two files added in one drop both see the first).
exports.signature: <T>(value: T | undefined, defaultValue: T, onChange?: (next: T) => void) => readonly [T, (next: T) => void, () => T]

exports.name: useFileDrop
exports.description: Takes OS file drops on one zone; `enabled: false` leaves every drag to the browser.

exports.name: FileDrop
exports.description: The two refs that take OS file drops: one on a stable ancestor for the bridge, one on the drop zone.

exports.name: useStickToBottom
exports.description: Keeps a scroller pinned to its newest content while the reader is at the bottom; `away` drives a jump-to-latest button.

exports.name: StickToBottomController
exports.description: The refs, state and actions that keep a scroller pinned to its newest content.
exports.typeParameters: <S extends HTMLElement = HTMLDivElement, C extends HTMLElement = HTMLDivElement>

exports.name: AI_CHAT_KEYBOARD_CATEGORY

exports.name: useScopedShortcut
exports.description:
Binds `shortcut` while mounted and `enabled`, firing only while focus is inside `scopeRef`'s
element. The handler is always the latest one; the binding is redone only when the key changes.
The kit's default input policy applies, so a plain key such as F2 does not fire inside a text field.
exports.signature: (part: string, scopeRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>, shortcut: AiChatShortcut, enabled?: boolean) => void

exports.description:
The one seam to a backend. Anything that can turn a request into an async stream of chunks works:
a fetch to an SSE endpoint, a WebSocket, a local model, the scripted fake. Stop is the `signal`
aborting; an adapter should end its iterator promptly when it does.

exports.description: Builds a thread from a linear list (each message's parentId must point at the one before).
